headline: High: shared filesystem and shell-capable A can leak or corrupt data when paired with local audio-only B, while B’s lack of write/network tools limits direct escalation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can read/write the filesystem and parse files or notebook content, so malicious content could influence it if B’s outputs are manually bridged into A. B has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, or file-writing capability, so there is no default automated injection channel between them.
conditions: IF an operator copies B-generated text into A’s notebook or file inputs
IF A is configured to treat file contents as instructions
mitigations: Keep B outputs out of A’s prompt/files unless reviewed
Use a fixed prompt template for A
Disable manual copy-paste between agents
Add a human approval step before A consumes B text

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches configuration secrets and can write/read files, but B cannot read files, use the network, or emit API calls. That makes direct leakage from A to B unlikely by default; the main risk is operator-mediated transfer of sensitive A outputs into B’s audio workflow.
conditions: IF sensitive A artifacts are manually transcribed into B inputs
IF B is wrapped by an external service that records transcripts
mitigations: Redact secrets before any handoff to B
Do not feed A logs into B
Store A secrets in separate files with restricted access
Review transcripts for sensitive content before retention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has shell, subprocess, filesystem write, and allowlisted egress; B is command-line only with no write or network. They do not obviously contend for the same mutable resource, but if both are pointed at the same workspace, A can overwrite files that B later consumes. Uncertainty about shared state pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same writable directory
IF B consumes files produced by A without locking
mitigations: Use separate working directories
Mount B read-only
Add file locks around shared artifacts
Serialize A and B access to shared inputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate research outputs and API responses, and B can be used as a downstream transcription/processing step. If B treats A’s text as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect speech or summaries. B has no built-in verification or network checks, so the pair lacks a default validation barrier.
conditions: IF B is fed A-generated text without verification
IF downstream users rely on B’s transcription or narration as factual
mitigations: Require a verification pass before B consumes A output
Mark A-generated text as untrusted metadata
Compare B output against source text
Add a human review step for high-stakes content

E_compliance.rationale: A handles configuration secrets and academic/research data, while B handles audio/speech. If regulated or sensitive content is spoken into B, the pair can create a residency or retention mismatch because B’s profile shows no explicit privacy controls, while A’s repo requests secrets and local development handling. The evidence is incomplete, so I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated audio or personal data is processed through B
IF A secrets or research data are spoken aloud and retained in transcripts
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to B
Set transcript retention to minimum
Separate secret-bearing A workflows from audio workflows
Document data-class handling for both agents
